findings.detail: The comment `# Skipping the pattern-list lines themselves, now that the file is in scope.` describes behaviour that does not exist — the grep on the next line (`list_scan_targets | xargs -0 -r grep -IHnE "$p"`) has no exclusion for this file or for the `patterns=(...)` block. It directly contradicts the block this PR just rewrote (lines 115-128), which correctly argues the opposite: no skipping is needed because none of the patterns match their own literal text. This matters here specifically because the whole point of the diff is to make the self-scan reasoning survive a future pattern being added — leaving a comment 30 lines below that says the lines are skipped invites the next author to trust a guard that isn't there and skip the per-pattern self-match check the new block asks for. Flagged as low, not medium, because the scanner's behaviour is correct; only the comment is wrong. It would rise to medium if the false comment were load-bearing for a caller.
findings.summary: Stale comment claims pattern-list lines are skipped; nothing skips them
